Unfortunately, I'm too attached to go back and burn the whole thing down.My personal vision of Middle-earth has always been something of a Victorian-medieval mash-up: late-medieval clothing and setting, but with Victorian gardens, food, domestic rhythms, and social concerns tucked into the corners.For the Beornings, I took a lot of inspiration from Norse culture, especially in the names, furniture, and household details. I relied heavily on Anna Arquette’s essay “Beornings and Woodmen” for information regarding Beorning culture. I also borrowed from selkie myths and other folklore about skinchangers. In this story, Beorn’s transformation is tied to a magical bearskin that he puts on to change.For what I'm sure are many inaccuracies, forgive me. I wrote what wanted to come out.
